chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The dog of the Magian (Zoroastrian) — do not eat its game unless the Muslim takes it, teaches it, and sends it; and likewise the falcon. And the dogs of the People of the Covenant (Dhimmi) and their falcons are permissible for Muslims to eat their game.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And from the game of the falcon, the hawk, and the cheetah, one does not eat except that which its slaughter is caught (i.e., consumed immediately). What was narrated indicates this.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating game hunted by Zoroastrians or People of the Covenant?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the permissibility of consuming game hunted by Magians and People of the Covenant, establishing that their dogs and falcons are valid hunters for Muslims provided the animal is slaughtered by a Muslim or the hunting process is properly initiated. Al-Sheikh al-Tusi’s commentary clarifies the condition for birds of prey, emphasizing that the meat is only lawful if the Muslim catches the slaughter (or the moment of death) to ensure the ritual validity of the hunt. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of extending the permissibility of non-Muslim hunters to include specific groups while maintaining the requirement of proper slaughter.
